text:
Maya (support): Customer (finance-platform) reports a sudden spike of 502/504 from hosted inference endpoints over the last 6 minutes. They see TLS handshake timeouts in their logs and our gateway is surfacing `upstream error` for multiple regions. Pasting their snippet:

Customer logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z ERROR api.gateway: handshake timeout after 10s, remote=api.redwood-hosted.net:443
2026-03-15T14:02:15Z WARN  resolver: SERVFAIL for cust.example.com -> fallback
2026-03-15T14:03:01Z ERROR http: upstream 502 gateway_error
```

Maya (support): They noticed it started right after a cert rotation initiated from the edge control plane (notified at 14:00) and also called out DNS flaps for their custom cname. Customer is blocked — requests failing end-to-end. Escalating. :rotating_light: @Noah can you pick this up?

Noah (oncall): I'm looking. First pass: is this affecting many customers or single-tenant routes? Any pattern by region? Can you drop the full request_id?

Maya (support): It's concentrated on their hosted route (cust-fin-prod) across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. I have request ids: `req_3f2a`, `req_3f2b`, `req_3f2c` — attaching packet capture they provided.

Ali (eng-network): Copying in. From attach: I see repeated TCP retrans and TLS ClientHello retrans until timeout. Looks like resolver returned intermittent NX/TIMEOUT then SERVFAIL, causing our gateway to attempt alternative upstreams, which then hit cert mismatch (SNI). Two possible things: (1) resolver instability causing upstream to flip, (2) cert rotation created a short window where SNI didn't line up with upstream instances.

Sam (sre): Can someone run a quick dig + tcptraceroute from an edge node to the customer's CNAME and to upstream model host? I want to rule out peering flaps.

Noah (oncall): Running from gw-usw2-21:
```
$ dig +short cust.example.com @8.8.8.8
67.215.45.90
$ dig +short cust.example.com @our-resolver
SERVFAIL
$ tcptraceroute cust.example.com 443
1 10.0.0.1 0.9 ms
2 52.88.12.45 2.1 ms
3 67.215.45.90 1200.4 ms  (hangs, retrans)
```

Noah (oncall): That 1200ms is consistent with the handshake timeouts. Looks like our internal resolver is returning SERVFAIL intermittently. Could be rate-limited or blackholed.

Ali (eng-network): Can we confirm whether the internal resolver rotation happened around the control plane cert rollout? I recall a resolver pool restart at 13:59 for config push. If the resolver push restarted processes and the edge cert rollout bumped SNI strings, there could be a two-factor timing issue. I'm going to pull resolver logs.

deploy-bot: resolver-service v2.14.1 deploy triggered by config/push at 2026-03-15T13:59:06Z (id: deploy-98342). Canary on 5 nodes.

Ali (eng-network): Confirmed. Resolver logs show `overloaded lookup queue` and repeated `SERVFAIL` between 14:01:30-14:04:00 while restart concurrent with cache flush. Also saw `EDNS0 malformed` from a subset of upstream stubs (isp-peers).

Sam (sre): Ok that maps. Operational impact: edge tried to resolve CNAME, got SERVFAIL -> fell back to alternative upstream (internal model host) which for some requests had in-flight cert that didn't yet present the new chain -> handshake fails -> downstream 502/504. Short term mitigation options: (A) re-route affected route to a stable resolver (fallback public) OR (B) increase gateway handshake timeout/retry backoff for cust-fin-prod to mask transient resolver hiccups. Which is lowest blast radius?

Noah (oncall): (A) is low-effort: point resolver for the edge node to 1.1.1.1 temporarily for that route. But that loses internal cache benefits and could increase latency slightly. (B) is also simple: bump handshake timeout from 10s to 20s for that route via runtime flag. Either needs approval.

Maya (support): Customer prefers quick fix — they asked for reduced errors now, even if latency slightly worse. Approve route to public resolver. I'll ask them to expect slightly higher p95.

Ali (eng-network): I'll patch edge config for the route to use fallback resolvers and restart name-resolve agent on the affected nodes. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: initiated hotpatch edge-resolver-fallback for service gw-usw2 (nodes 21-25) at 2026-03-15T14:07:45Z.

Noah (oncall): After hotpatch, customer reports success: 14:09 onwards request success rates back to normal. I still see degraded p95 latency ~150ms more.

Maya (support): Customer confirms 200s ok, thanks. They're okay with the temporary latency.

Ali (eng-network): Root cause summary for postmortem: resolver restart + cache flush during a control-plane cert rollout caused transient SERVFAILs and inconsistent DNS answers from some upstream stubs. That triggered upstream host churn and exposed in-flight cert rotation mismatch (SNI) on some model hosts leading to handshake timeouts and gateway 5xxs.

Sam (sre): Long term fixes proposed: 1) coordinate resolver restarts out of cert rotation windows, 2) add graceful cache warm-up + backoff to resolver restarts, 3) ensure cert rollouts are idempotent across old/new SNI names (grace period), 4) add route-level automatic fallback to public resolvers if internal resolver SERVFAIL rate exceeds X within Y seconds.

Maya (support): I'll file the incident ticket and include customer impact, timeline, and the suggested mitigations. Assigning follow-ups to @Ali and @Sam for permanent changes.

Ali (eng-network): I'll own the resolver warm-up plan and add a canary gate for config pushes.

Sam (sre): I'll add the alert for resolver SERVFAIL rate and a runbook to auto-fallback routes after X failures.

Noah (oncall): Closing real-time channel. If any regression ping here and I'll reopen. Great cross-team response, saved the customer quickly. :white_check_mark:
